hypothesis: The generic blanket ban on externally constrained groups prevents useful HDMI/UART alternatives.
prototype: Allow explicitly selected wired groups with only finite nonnegative near_max bounds and resolved targets into generic orientation and contract-group candidate generation. Preserve actual external terms, local contract checks and per-shape metrics.
disposition: Removed after no additional HDMI or UART offers were demonstrated. Production candidate-generation source restored; retain regression coverage and evidence only.
finding: The templated stage builder already supplies four HDMI rigid orientations independently of generic orientation eligibility. Its external-contract exclusion must not be mistaken for a ban on all alternative HDMI orientations. Lifting that exclusion alone did not resolve smaller-board placement.
regression_coverage: Both-board orientation suite; HDMI incumbent offers preserved, actual shape metrics transported, HDMI near_max to som_j2 remains enforced at frozen-fixture bound 10 mm, UART near_max to usb_uart_connector remains enforced at frozen-fixture bound 40 mm. These tests verify transport, not authoritative physical justification of those numeric bounds. No maximum candidate count imposed.
scope: Six single-run prepared-input construction screens. No new full qualification, smaller board, controlled speedup or Python timing comparison. Search exhaustion is not geometric infeasibility.
next: Investigate joint shape selection and translation, including floating-point separation endpoint construction. Review authored judgment bounds against hardware evidence separately; neither an inherited heuristic nor a search effort limit establishes a physical minimum board size. Preserve valid incumbents and retain all actual search-work receipts.
